title: Canara Bank - 532483 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Canara Bank Q2 FY27: record quarterly net profit of ₹5,175 crore (+8.40% YoY) with Gross NPA down to 1.33%, while ECL transition provisioning now seen at ₹12,000–15,000 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported total business crossing ₹30 lakh crore (+15.88% YoY), advances +19.46% and deposits +13.13%, with NII up 20.39% and NIM at 2.53% annual / 2.55% quarterly. Asset quality improved further: Gross NPA 1.33%, Net NPA 0.30%, PCR 95.34% (+175 bps YoY), annualised slippage 0.58% and credit cost 0.47%. Treasury turned into a loss versus the prior year, with MTM about ₹600 crore lower QoQ for the quarter, and management flagged the RBI ECL transition as a ₹12,000–15,000 crore one-time provision requirement. CASA at 29% was the only guidance miss, which management attributed to ₹55,000 crore of FCNR(B) deposits.

financial_highlights.change: FY27 guidance was 1.50% GNPA and ~0.40% NNPA
Agri ₹687 cr, MSME ₹777 cr, Retail ₹327 cr, Corporate ₹13 cr, Gold ₹40 cr

financial_highlights.value: loss of ₹61 crore in Q2 (Q1 was profit ₹654 crore; cumulative H1 ~₹593 crore)
financial_highlights.change: Q2 FY26 MTM profit was ₹762 crore

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail credit grew 31.61% YoY and housing 17.35% (other figures cited: total retail ~21%, housing 17–18%); vehicle loans +25.50%. Management said retail-related margin is 8.65% of earnings.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 21.03% YoY; MSME +15.49% YoY; Retail slippages ₹327 crore and MSME slippages ₹777 crore in Q2.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Total agri ₹3.04 lakh crore: gold agri ₹1.74 lakh crore (~₹1.51 lakh crore QoQ) and core agri ₹1.30 lakh crore (~₹1.25 lakh crore QoQ), core agri growing about 9%. Agri slippages ₹687 crore.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loans ₹2.82 lakh crore (agri ₹1.74 lakh crore, non-agri ₹1.08 lakh crore). Incremental gold yield rose to 9.10% from 8.96% QoQ; gold slippages ₹40 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Incremental corporate yield 7.72% vs 7.68% in Q1; ~₹47,000–50,000 crore of sanctioned-not-disbursed plus hot leads (₹30,000 crore hot leads, ₹17,000 crore sanctioned) in power, green energy, BESS, data centres and HAM roads.

segments.name: Treasury / investments
segments.commentary: Investment book 80% HTM and ~20% AFS/FVTPL; AFS losses ~₹1,300 crore for the quarter go to AFS reserve, not P&L; FVTPL <4% of book. Yields hardened 44 bps in the quarter, ~₹600 crore MTM hit (QoQ basis).

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Canbank Factors stake sale done: ₹14 crore investment, expected ~4x return. Canara HSBC Life and Canara Robeco AMC are listed in the plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (set at start of year): total business +10–11% (delivered +15.88%), advances +11–12% (delivered +19.46%), deposits +9–10% (delivered +13.13%), CASA 30–32% (delivered 29%), NIM 2.50–2.60%, ROE 16.5%, EPS ₹20, ROA 1.01–1.05%; management said it does not plan to revise guidance and will try to better it.

NIM expected to sustain around 2.55% and the 25 bps repo hike is in the book; 53% of the book is repo-linked and already repriced. FCNR(B) leverage spread of only 40–50 bps is expected to be compensated from Q3.

ECL transition one-time provision now estimated at ₹12,000–15,000 crore (up from ₹10,000–12,000 crore), including HTM; management sees up to ₹14,000–15,000 crore if yields stay hardened, with possible return to ₹10,000–12,000 crore if oil prices and geopolitics ease. Impact about 1–1.2% of CRAR/CET1 basis; spread over 1–2 years (5-year option allowed, but not expected).

Management does not expect the ECL provision to materially hit ROA; it said ROA could settle near 0.80% if provisions are not passed on, but would be above 1% if passed through. No decision yet on passing through.
Management expects to complete ECL model dry run within the current quarter (before 31 March 2027 deadline).
capex_capacity: Capex/capacity disclosure is absent: no capex plan, branch or technology spend figures were given; management said it is investing heavily in digital advancements (QR, school fee modules, internet payment gateways) without quantification.
Balance sheet capacity: CRAR 17.19% and CET1 12.80% vs regulatory minimums of 11.5% and 8.5%; management said RWA density is falling quarter-on-quarter.
ECL model build: dry run with technology partner Coforge expected within the current quarter, ahead of the 31 March 2027 deadline.
Liquidity: LCR 115% as of 30 September 2026; FCNR(B) raised $5.8 billion (~₹55,000 crore), of which $3.2 billion funded advances and the rest replaced bulk deposits.

Lending pipeline: ₹17,000 crore sanctioned but not disbursed plus ₹30,000 crore hot leads (~₹47,000–50,000 crore) in power, green energy, BESS, data centres and HAM roads; ECLGS disbursement ₹13,000+ crore.
demand_pricing: Retail demand robust with festive season; housing growth 17–18% and total retail ~21%; vehicle loans +25%; management says festive mode already started before Dussehra.
Gold loans: competition rising from large NBFCs; management says Canara prices below NBFCs (which borrow from banks) and sees gold yields rising further as rates harden.

Deposit cost: bulk deposits held at ~₹4.38 lakh crore (vs ₹4.37 lakh crore in Q1). FCNR(B) raised $5.8 billion (~₹55,000 crore), of which $3.2 billion funded advances and the rest replaced bulk deposits; overall cost of deposits lower by ~1%.
Drought: 3 states declared drought-affected (part of Karnataka and Maharashtra cited); exposure ~₹13,900 crore; restructuring to be handled via SLBC dispensation.
Digital fee income: UPI MDR not yet quantified; ai1Pe PSP platform has limited traction; management sees little fee upside currently.

qa_highlights.question: What are incremental yields on corporate and gold loans, and will NIM improve from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate incremental yield 7.72% (vs 7.68% Q1); gold 9.10% (vs 8.96%). Management expects NIM to hold around 2.55% with 53% of the book already repriced and MCLR resets to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bulk deposit flat if FCNR(B) was raised; what is the NIM offset?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) fully replaced bulk deposits and saved ~100 bps on the replaced portion (6.5% vs 7.5%) plus CRR/SLR cost benefits. Bulk held at ₹4.38 lakh crore; the FCNR leverage spread (40–50 bps) should be offset from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL one-time provision and how will it hit net worth and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimate ₹12,000–15,000 crore including HTM (RBI allows 5 years). Management prefers to spread over 1–2 years; expects PCR to rise to 96–97% and profit >₹20,000 crore to absorb it without denting ROA.

qa_highlights.question: Will the drought affect recoveries and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Drought exposure is ~₹13,900 crore; SLBC restructuring/moratorium expected. Total stress including SMA-0 is 2.42% (₹33,340 crore); >₹5 crore tickets stress 0.30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury/MTM impact and AFS reserve position?
qa_highlights.answer: AFS losses ~₹1,300 crore go to reserve; FVTPL loss ~₹600 crore QoQ swing (Q1 +₹555 crore, Q2 -₹55 crore). Yields hardened 44 bps in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Canbank Factors sale and recovery trend on written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Canbank Factors sale done (₹14 crore cost, ~4x expected). Written-off pool ~₹18,000 crore and dwindling; recoveries exceed slippages each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: SMA position and LCR?
qa_highlights.answer: SMA 0–2 for ≥₹5 crore is 0.51% (₹7,043 crore); SMA 2 is 0.21% and SMA 1 0.09%. LCR 115% at 30 Sep 2026.

risks_watch: ECL one-time provision of ₹12,000–15,000 crore (up from ₹10,000–12,000 crore); a dry run is due this quarter and the phasing decision (1–2 years vs 5-year option) is deferred to the last quarter.
Bond yield path: management said yields could harden further, with HTM also subject to provisioning; a 44 bps hardening in Q2 drove the treasury swing.
Whether ECL provisions are passed on to customers: ROA could settle near 0.80% if not passed on, above 1% if passed through; no decision yet.
Gold loan competition from large NBFCs; management expects no yield pressure but acknowledged rising competition.
CASA at 29% vs 30–32% guidance; FCNR(B) leverage spread of only 40–50 bps to be offset from Q3, and the bulk deposit replacement may need to continue.
Drought exposure ~₹13,900 crore across 3 states; restructuring depends on state-level SLBC dispensations.
key_quotes: So, we have no plan to evaluate, Sir.
Our Housing loan in excess of 17%, 18% is growing. Total retail, 21%, vehicle loan, 25%.
Even if we are not passing, then ROA will be not, say, in excess of 1%. Then new normal will become 80 basis points, you see.
That market will decide. As of now, we do not see much of movement out of that also.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, growth and capital, with management saying it has no plan to revise FY27 guidance and will try to better it. Cautious and non-committal on the ECL timing and pass-through decision, the treasury outlook and the bond yield path, where answers were repeatedly "that market will decide" or "premature to say".

growth.why: FY27 total business guide was +10–11% (delivered +15.88% YoY, advances +19.46% vs 11–12% guide), with management saying it will not revise guidance and will aim to beat it; backing is partial, citing ₹47,000–50,000 crore sanctioned-not-disbursed plus hot leads and robust retail demand, but no company capacity additions were disclosed.
